title: Kyoto in five days
summary: Five days from Fushimi Inari and Tofuku-ji to Arashiyama and the Kamo River, with neighbourhood routes, rainy-day options and room in the budget. Check current access and menus before travelling.

sections.heading: The five-day order
sections.content: Group five days by area: Fushimi Inari and Tofuku-ji; Kiyomizu-dera and the hillside lanes; Arashiyama; Nishiki Market and central Kyoto; then a short Kamo River walk before departure. Leave about an hour free after lunch. Kyoto Station suits luggage and rail connections; Shijo-Kawaramachi suits evening walks. Keep one base and check room size, luggage arrangements and the real station walk.

sections.heading: Temples and paths need time
sections.content: Pair Fushimi Inari with Tofuku-ji. The Inari summit is optional; wet temple steps call for grippy shoes. Kiyomizu-dera has uphill approaches. In Arashiyama, combine bamboo and Togetsukyo Bridge, choose stations first, then decide on Tenryu-ji. Store large bags and keep paths open when photographing.

sections.heading: Transport and a flexible budget
sections.content: Map the actual day before choosing rail, subway, buses or walking. Check Arashiyama operators and stations; a pass helps only when it covers planned rides. An initial daily local-transport allowance around a thousand yen should be replaced with actual fares. Fix accommodation and intercity travel first, split a shared room once, separate shopping and leave a contingency around ten percent. Rounded amounts are planning allowances, not live quotations.

sections.heading: Food and markets along the way
sections.content: Tofu, soba or a set meal can end a walking day without another cross-city trip. Allow roughly a couple of thousand yen per person with flexibility, then use the menu. Ask staff directly about ingredients and preparation. At Nishiki Market, browse before buying, collect ceramics later and check individual stalls. Verify destination import rules before taking food home.

sections.heading: Keep rainy days shorter
sections.content: Swap a long outdoor walk for Kyoto National Museum or central cafés and covered Nishiki Market in heavy rain. Check exhibitions, closure dates and admission. Follow stalls’ eating instructions and keep passages clear. Return to your accommodation for dry socks rather than filling every hour.

sections.heading: What to carry
sections.content: Carry water, folding umbrella, power bank and a light layer, with grippy shoes. Save accommodation, return service and a daily map offline; back up photographs at night. Keep payment items reachable. Wrap tea, ceramics and camera gear separately.

sections.heading: The river and the journey home
sections.content: Join the Kamo River near Sanjo or Shijo for roughly half an hour to an hour. Sitting by the water counts. Turn back at flooding or closure notices and identify a return station. On departure day, default to breakfast near Kyoto Station. Confirm platform, luggage and collection time before a bakery detour; protect the train journey.
